title: New Underground Electric Service System
description: Install and energize a new main distribution cabinet and new Hydro Quebec (HQ) Site Service. Provide the necessary power pedestals and connection points for temporary event connections. title: RFP FOR FIRST LINE OF DEFENCE SECURITY SOLUTION

title: Mobile Treatment Center
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) The Department of National Defence (DND), in support of the Canadian Forces Health Services (CFHS), has a requirement for the supply, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning, documentation, and warranty support of ten (10) Mobile Treatment Centre (MTC) cap-style slide-in modules. The MTCs will be installed on Government-owned 2024 Dodge RAM 3500 trucks and will provide enhanced casualty treatment, extraction, and transportation capabilities to support CFHS training, routine operations, mandated safety activities, and domestic response operations across Canada. The requirement includes all associated equipment, components, installation harnesses, medical treatment accommodations, electrical and environmental systems, emergency warning equipment, documentation, training, and services necessary to deliver a fully operational capability. The resulting contract will be effective from the date of contract award until March 31, 2028. The initial requirement includes the firm supply, delivery, installation, testing, and commissioning of two (2) Mobile Treatment Centre (MTC) units. Canada will have the option to acquire up to eight (8) additional MTC units, which may be exercised, in whole or in part, at any time during the two-year contract period. Delivery and installation are required at the locations identified in Appendix 1 to Annex Statement of Requirements. Offers will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation criteria set out in the solicitation documents. The contract will be awarded to the responsive Offeror whose Offer achieves the highest combined rating of technical merit and price. The requirement is subject to the Interim Policy on Reciprocal Procurement. Supplier eligibility will be determined in accordance with the requirements set out in the solicitation documents. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. NOTE TO BIDDERS: Procurement Assistance Canada offers seminars to businesses interested in learning how to sell goods and services to the Government of Canada. The seminars are FREE.

description: Kerry Education and Training Board (Kerry ETB), through Kerry College Monavalley Campus, invites tenders for the supply, refurbishment for training use, delivery and full installation of one (1) decommissioned wind turbine nacelle, complete with drivetrain and auxiliary systems, for use as a static training asset. The successful supplier shall be responsible for providing a complete, safe and fully installed equipment solution, including all labour, supervision, plant, lifting arrangements, fixings, accessories, connections, testing and handover necessary for the intended training use. The nacelle will be used to deliver practical training on the Wind Turbine Maintenance Technician apprenticeship and related further education and training programmes. It will not be returned to power-generating service. The asset must therefore be safe, fully accessible, and representative of the equipment apprentices will encounter in industry. This specification is drafted on a brand-neutral basis in accordance with public procurement rules (Directive 2014/24/EU and S.I. No. 284 of 2016). No reference to a specific make or model is intended or implied. Where a functional or dimensional characteristic is stated, equipment of any manufacturer meeting that characteristic is acceptable.

title: Ireland – Design consultancy services – Request for Tender for the Provision of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content
description: The Commission is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified service provider for the design, management and delivery of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content. The successful Tenderer will be required to design, manage and deliver a structured programme of talent development and content development activities that strengthen professional capability within the audiovisual sector, facilitate collaboration between practitioners across the island of Ireland and support the development of high-quality audiovisual projects aligned with the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund. The services to be provided include, but are not limited to: • designing and delivering a structured programme of workshops, masterclasses, mentoring, networking events and audiovisual content development activities; • developing and implementing a fair, open and transparent recruitment and selection process for programme participants; • facilitating collaboration between audiovisual practitioners from across the island of Ireland, including participants from different jurisdictions, backgrounds and communities; • providing experienced facilitators, mentors and industry specialists to support participant learning and project development; • supporting participants in the development of audiovisual projects that demonstrate potential to progress to production and reflect the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund; • managing all aspects of programme delivery, stakeholder engagement, administration and communications; • monitoring programme delivery and performance against agreed milestones; and • providing progress reports, financial reporting and a final programme evaluation report in accordance with the requirements set out in Appendix 1 – Specification of Services.

title: France – Repair and maintenance services of cooler groups – Maintenance des installations de climatisation industrielle CM Lyon
description: Ce présent avis annule et replace l'avis 618889-2026. La présente consultation a pour objet la maintenance préventive et corrective (sur devis) des équipements de climatisation des postes électriques de RTE situés sur le territoire du centre Maintenance de Lyon. Le parc concerné représente environ 310 installations de climatisation installés dans des locaux industriels sensibles (salles de relayage, salles de télécommunication, bâtiments de commande). Le marché est alloti en 5 lots géographiques à la maille du Groupe Maintenance Réseaux du Centre Maintenance Lyon: lot 1 -Auvergne, lot 2 - Dauphiné, lot 3 - Forez-Velay, lot 4 - Lyonnais et lot 5 - Savoie. Chaque lot est attribué à un titulaire unique ; un même opérateur ne peut être attributaire de plus de 3 lots. Les candidats peuvent se positionner sur un, plusieurs ou l'ensemble des lots de leur choix. Les accords-cadres, d'une durée de 3 ans fermes (du 01/02/2027 au 31/01/2030) reconductibles 3 fois 1 an, sont conclus avec un engagement financier limité au volume de 2 années de maintenance préventive.

title: Water Intake Facility at Radford Army Ammunition Plant
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice for informational purposes only to determine the interest and availability of potential qualified contractors for a new Water Intake Facility at the Radford Army Ammuntion Plant (RFAAP). RFAAP, located in Radford, VA is a Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) production facility providing state-of-the-art propellants, energetics, and munitions to support the Warfighter. All production at RFAAP depends on river water. Completing construction to the supporting infrastructure and in-water work will ensure the continued operation of the primary water intake at RFAAP and resilience of water supply to the facility.

title: Minot Air Force Base Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) IDIQ
description: This is a Request for Proposal (RFP) for commercial, non-personal services prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 "Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services", Part 15 "Contracting by Negotiation", and Part 36 "Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts" procedures. This acquisition is 100% set aside for Small Business Concerns. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with this requirement is 236220 "Commercial and Institutional Building Construction". The Small Business Size Standard associated with this NAICS is $45,000,000.00. The 5th Contracting Squadron, Minot Air Force Base (AFB), North Dakota, is requesting proposals to establish the base award(s) for a Minot AFB Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) vehicle. The MACC IDIQ will fulfill a continuous and recurring need for a broad range of design-bid-build and design-build construction projects to support the missions of the 5th Bomb Wing, 91st Missile Wing, and multiple tenant units assigned to Minot AFB. There is no seed project included with this solicitation. The MACC will have an initial five (5)-year ordering period with one (1), five (5)-year optional ordering period. The total aggregate maximum amount expendable under the entire MACC lifecycle SHALL NOT EXCEED $500,000,000.00. The guaranteed minimum amount over the life of the MACC is $500.00. The awardees' guaranteed minimum will be satisfied by attendance at the MACC Post-Award Conference. NOTICE TO OFFERORS (AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS): Funds are not available for the minimum guarantee. Award under this solicitation is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. The complete solicitation package is available in this posting. Anyone wishing to participate in this proposed procurement must obtain their copy from this website. Copies will not be distributed from the Contracting Office. All amendments will be posted on SAM.gov. Contractors are solely responsible for obtaining amendments from this site to update files. The complete solicitation package includes eight (8) attachments: 1. MACC Statement of Work 2. MACC Ordering Guide 3. MACC Specifications 4. Section L - Instructions to Offerors 5. Section M - Evaluation Factors for Award 6. Davis-Bacon Act Wage Determinations 7. Financial Responsibility Authorization Letter 8. Subcontractor Consent Letter NOTICE TO OFFERORS (MANDATORY SAM REGISTRATION): All prospective contractors must be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) at time of receipt of proposals. Failure to be active and registered in SAM will cause your firm to be ineligible for award. Offerors are highly encouraged to thoroughly review all solicitation documents prior to submitting their proposal. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by the agency. All contractors� questions in response to this solicitation must be emailed to 5CONS.PKA-C.MACC@us.af.mil no later than 31 August 2026 at 10:00 AM CDT. The Government will not be held responsible for answering any questions after this time. All questions/answers resulting from this solicitation will be posted to SAM.gov as an amendment.

description: The U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) - Fort Knox, 199 6th Avenue, Suite 250, Fort Knox, KY, 40121, intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to WCP/Fern Exposition Services, LLC. doing business as FERN (UEI: NBLRXSNYZPF8 I CAGE Code: 4E6D9), located at 645 Linn St, Cincinnati, OH 45203-1722. The procurement is to provide ancillary services to include furniture, carpet and carpet padding rental, cleaning, accessories, and material handling at the National Future Farmers of America (NFFA) 2026 Convention & Expo in Indianapolis, Indiana. The U.S. Army Recruiting Command (USAREC) requires chairs, tables/risers, carpet, accessories, draping, cleaning services, material handling, cartload services, and accessible storage. This action is being conducted under FAR Part 12 (DFARS CD 2026-000028), Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is simplified acquisition procedures for commercial products and commercial services, Title 41 U.S.C. 1901, as implemented by FAR 12.102(a) (DFARS CD 2026-00028), as only one source is available valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold. This is not a request for competitive offers, quotes, or capability statements. No solicitation will be posted as a result of this notice. This notice complies with FAR 5.101 (DFARS CD 2026-00003), Methods of disseminating information. However, interested parties may submit capability statements demonstrating their ability to meet this requirement within the required timeframe. All capability statements must be received no later than 28 September 2026, at 10:00 AM Eastern Time. Submitted capability statements shall include sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to meet the requirement, including relevant experience, pricing information (if available), and supporting documentation. Submissions shall be sent via email to Contract Specialist, Ashley Brus at ashley.a.brus.civ@army.mil and Contracting Officer, Meagan Clavel at meagan.s.clavel.civ@army.mil. The anticipated award date is October 2026.

title: SourcesSought_BaseWideFurnitureMaintenance2026
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS (Not a Notice of Solicitation) DESCRIPTION: Notice from the United States Air Force, Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Operational Contacting Division, Base Support Contracting Branch at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio: INTRODUCTION - The AFLCMC Operational Contracting Branch at Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio, on behalf of the 88th Civil Engineer Group, is conducting market research through a Sources Sought Notice to identify potential sources, including Small Businesses (SB), capable of providing Base-Wide Furniture Maintenance (BWFM), telecommunications, and minor interior finishing support at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio. This notice is for informational purposes only to determine the availability of qualified sources to support this requirement. A set-aside decision has not yet been made for this acquisition. Requirements: The 88th Civil Engineer Group (88 CEG) requires a contractor to provide all personnel, equipment, tools, and materials necessary to perform furniture maintenance, redesign, installation, and associated support services. The scope of work includes, but is not limited to, the following core requirements: Furniture Maintenance & Installation: Disassembly, reconfiguration, and installation of various systems furniture (e.g., Herman Miller, Steelcase, Haworth, Knoll). Computer-Aided Design (CAD): Providing 2D and 3D layout designs and Labor & Material (L&M) quotes. Warehousing & Inventory Management: Managing and conducting inventory of Government-owned furniture assets within a Government-furnished, on-site warehouse facility. Telecommunications & Data Cabling: Coordinating and executing the routing of communication lines through furniture, including adherence to WPAFB standards for CAT6 and non-CAT6 cabling. Ancillary Interior Services: Providing minor interior finishing services incidental to furniture reconfiguration, which may include patching/painting, minor plumbing, and electrical adjustments as required. Safeguarding Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): Adhering to strict policies for handling and storing facility floor plans. CAPABILITY STATEMENT REQUIREMENTS Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement (no more than 7 pages). The statement must address the contractor�s ability to perform the tasks outlined in the Scope of Work. Please include: Company Profile: Company name, address, POC, CAGE Code, UEI number, and socioeconomic status. Furniture & Design Expertise: A summary of experience with multi-manufacturer systems furniture and providing CAD layouts. Warehouse & Inventory Management: Your approach to managing a Government-furnished warehouse and inventory. Telecommunications & Ancillary Services (CRITICAL): A detailed explanation of how your company will execute the data cabling, electrical, plumbing, and painting requirements. Please specify whether this work will be performed by in-house technicians or through subcontracting/teaming agreements. Security Clearances: Confirmation of the ability to meet CUI safeguarding and base access requirements. Closing: RESPONSES ARE DUE NOT LATER THAN 28 September 2026 BY 10:30 AM EDT. Direct all questions concerning this acquisition to alisha.cvitkovich@us.af.mil. Responses may be submitted electronically to the following e-mail address: alisha.cvitkovich@us.af.mil and andrew.petersen.3@us.af.mil. All correspondence sent via email shall contain a subject line that reads "Base Wide Furniture Maintenance Follow-On." This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overall (RFO) 15.101, responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Any information submitted by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary and will not be reimbursed by the Government. The Government�s assessment of the capability statements received will factor in whether any forthcoming solicitation will be conducted as a full and open competition or as a set-aside. title: Airfield Civil Works IDIQ
description: This is the official solicitation for the Tyndall Air Force Base Airfield Civil Works Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) requirement. The points of contact (POCs) for this pre-solicitation are SrA Frances Montgomery at (850)283-8640 or frances.motngomery@us.af.mil, Mr. Joseph Petersen at (850)283-8618 or joseph.petersen.3@us.af.mil, and Mrs. Tanya Gutka at (850)283-8650 or tanya.gutka@us.af.mil. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and the Product Service Code (PSC) Z2BD Repair or Alteration of Airport Runways and Taxiways Services. The small business size standard under NAICS 237310 is $45,000,000.00. The Department of the Air Force anticipates issuing a solicitation for a comprehensive Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to execute various civil works projects on the active airfield at Tyndall AFB where specific requirements and quantities will be established via individual Task Orders throughout the five-year ordering period (base year and four option years). The scope of work encompasses the demolition, repair, and new construction of heavy-load airfield pavements, including Portland Cement Concrete (PCC), Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA), and interlocking pavers. Associated civil infrastructure tasks include earthwork, subgrade preparation, and grading. Key Operational and Environmental Constraints: This requirement necessitates operating within a highly restricted, active military flightline environment. The successful contractor must possess the proven capability to: Execute complex construction phasing that minimizes operational downtime for active runways and taxiways; maintain rigorous flightline safety protocols; including comprehensive Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and dynamic coordination with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and Airfield Management; achieve strict adherence to Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) for heavy aircraft loading and DoD safety manual EM 385-1-1; manage complex environmental compliance; including securing Environmental Resource Permits (ERP) and safely handling, containing, and disposing of contaminated soils and groundwater, specifically in areas impacted by Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF). All potential offerors will submit proposals through the PIEE Solicitation module. Proposals are due NLT 28 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT. Questions are due NLT 08 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT.

title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. title: Airfield Civil Works IDIQ
description: This is the official solicitation for the Tyndall Air Force Base Airfield Civil Works Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) requirement. The points of contact (POCs) for this pre-solicitation are SrA Frances Montgomery at (850)283-8640 or frances.motngomery@us.af.mil, Mr. Joseph Petersen at (850)283-8618 or joseph.petersen.3@us.af.mil, and Mrs. Tanya Gutka at (850)283-8650 or tanya.gutka@us.af.mil. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and the Product Service Code (PSC) Z2BD Repair or Alteration of Airport Runways and Taxiways Services. The small business size standard under NAICS 237310 is $45,000,000.00. The Department of the Air Force anticipates issuing a solicitation for a comprehensive Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to execute various civil works projects on the active airfield at Tyndall AFB where specific requirements and quantities will be established via individual Task Orders throughout the five-year ordering period (base year and four option years). The scope of work encompasses the demolition, repair, and new construction of heavy-load airfield pavements, including Portland Cement Concrete (PCC), Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA), and interlocking pavers. Associated civil infrastructure tasks include earthwork, subgrade preparation, and grading. Key Operational and Environmental Constraints: This requirement necessitates operating within a highly restricted, active military flightline environment. The successful contractor must possess the proven capability to: Execute complex construction phasing that minimizes operational downtime for active runways and taxiways; maintain rigorous flightline safety protocols; including comprehensive Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and dynamic coordination with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and Airfield Management; achieve strict adherence to Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) for heavy aircraft loading and DoD safety manual EM 385-1-1; manage complex environmental compliance; including securing Environmental Resource Permits (ERP) and safely handling, containing, and disposing of contaminated soils and groundwater, specifically in areas impacted by Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF). All potential offerors will submit proposals through the PIEE Solicitation module. Proposals are due NLT 28 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT. Questions are due NLT 08 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT.

A site visit is planned for this solicitation. The estimated magnitude of this construction project is between $250,000 and $500,000.

title: Ireland – Software package and information systems – UL1084 Enterprise-level Systematic Review Management Platform to the University of Limerick
description: University of Limerick is seeking to procure an enterprise-level, cloud-based Systematic Review Management Platform to support researchers, academics, students, librarians and research support staff in conducting high-quality evidence synthesis activities across the institution. The proposed solution must provide an integrated end-to-end workflow for systematic reviews and related evidence synthesis methodologies, including citation management, screening, full-text review, data extraction, risk of bias assessment, collaboration, reporting and publication-ready outputs. The platform should facilitate efficient collaboration between internal and external researchers, provide enterprise-grade administration and reporting capabilities, and support recognised methodologies such as systematic reviews, scoping reviews, rapid reviews, mixed-methods reviews and meta-analyses. The successful Tenderer will be required to deliver a fully managed Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, including implementation, training, ongoing support, systematic review methodological expertise, security and compliance assurances, and enterprise-level service management. The solution must align with the University's information governance, security, accessibility and architectural requirements, while providing value for money and supporting the University's strategic ambition to strengthen research excellence and evidence-informed decision-making across the institution.

title: RRSA 20V1163TB93L Diesel Engine Disassembly and Parts Harvesting
description: The U.S. Coast Guard has a one-time requirement for services associated with four MTU series 20V1163TB93L diesel engines currently stored at a Rolls-Royce Solutions America facility in Brownstown, Michigan. The requirement includes the following major tasks: Transport and complete disassembly of four MTU 20V1163TB93L diesel engines. Salvage of usable spare parts to support the National Security Cutter fleet. Salvage of all four crankshafts. Modification of two salvaged crankshafts to the current approved/improved radius design. Cleaning, preservation, packaging, and marking of salvaged components for long-term storage and future fleet use. Preservation, sealing, packaging, and shipment of two bare engine blocks for long-term strategic storage. Scrapping and disposal of two bare engine blocks. Inventory, sorting, preservation, and disposition of parts contained in Government-owned conex sea containers. Shipment of project deliverables FOB Destination to Government-designated locations. The engines identified for disassembly are: Engine Serial Number 5840363 Engine Serial Number 5840364 Engine Serial Number 5840397 Engine Serial Number 5840401 The salvaged parts will support sustainment of the U.S. Coast Guard National Security Cutter Main Propulsion Diesel Engines. Evidence of capability to perform or obtain approved crankshaft machining/modification to the current approved design.. title: PTAG RFI: USPTO seeks Contractor to Review and Revise the Patent Examiner Training program.
description: THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY.? It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the?solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under PSC U008 - EDUCATION/TRAINING- TRAINING/CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT and NAICS: 611430 - Professional and Management Development Training REQUEST FOR INFORMATION � PTA TRAINING CONSULTATION, ELEARNING & DELIVERY BACKGROUND The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) intends to make a firm-fixed price award to a single firm that can fulfill this requirement which includes three (3) major elements. Training Consultation for Program Revision; Development of eLearning Content; Training Delivery Support Services. USPTO�s Patent Training Academy is the training program responsible for preparing new hires to be patent examiners. It is designed to give new examiners the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to begin their careers. In FY 2026, USPTO hired 963 new examiners. Currently, the training program is delivered over 10-weeks and is comprised of a 125-course curriculum. The program follows a university-style model that uses a mix of large-lectures and small group lab sessions to give examiners opportunity to apply what they have learned. Through a combination of the use of a practice training application, active learning exercises, lecture and dedicated examination time, the goal of the program is to provide patent examiner new-hires the needed competencies to successfully examine in a Technology Center (TC) with guidance from experienced examiners. OBJECTIVE The objective of this RFI is to seek capable contractors who could provide the USPTO with Training Consultation for Program Revision, Development of eLearning Content, and Training Delivery Support Services. REQUIREMENTS: Training Consultation for Program Revision: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in instructional design consultation services, to include: Expertise in instructional design and adult learning theories and principles. Experience providing solutions to enhance engagement and learning in large training programs with extensive curriculums, specifically more than 40 courses in a single curriculum. Experience with providing innovative solutions including AI to enhance learning and taking complex, detailed curriculum and transforming the curriculum to provide faster acquisition of job skills and application of content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to refine learning objectives and ensure content alignment with learning objectives for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course activities for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course pedagogy for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to guide the assessment of learning objectives and outcomes. Experience in providing consultation services for legal content. As directed, develop training content and related deliverables. Development of eLearning Content: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the development and implementation of eLearning content, to include: Expertise in the design of eLearning content, using standard eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline 360, Adobe Captivate, etc. Expertise in incorporating instructional design and adult learning theories and principles to eLearning content. Experience in building in adaptive gamification into eLearning content. Experience in designing microlearning content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to ensure the design correctly represents legally accurate materials. Experience in incorporating clean visuals, graphics, and ensuring 508-compliance of all materials. Experience in graphic design, visual clarity, and technical writing to ensure clear instructions and flow of all eLearning content. Experience in intuitive, learner-centered design. Experience in clearly defining design processes, to include steps in design processes, timelines, and checkpoints for subject-matter expert review. Ability to convert 25 courses into eLearning modules in 3 months. Courses range from 1 hour to 2.5 hours� worth of content. Training Delivery Support Services: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the implementation of Training Delivery Support Services, to include: Experience providing training in person and online, using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Experience in ensuring best practices in engagement and adult learning theory are incorporated into training delivery. Ability to deliver training on all agency examination processes, procedures and tools accessing patent applications, in-house tools for searching US and Foreign Patents that allow examiners to generate correspondence to applicants, case management tools. Ability to deliver professional training that is consistent with USPTO standards to support professional development to USPTO patent examiner employees. The training must be conducted by a variety of means including in person, in a classroom or lecture setting, and/or using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Please state if you have specific experience with intellectual property (IP), patent examination, and patent prosecution processes. Experience in ensuring continuity in training to avoid re-scheduling of training classes. The ability to ensure training coverage for a schedule such as the one listed below: Phase 1 Week 1 8:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 2 8:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 3 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 4 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 5 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 6 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days Week 7 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 8 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days Week 9 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 10 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days PROGRAM TIMELINE Contractors would be expected to begin delivering consultation services in October 2026, with an expectation of revised training program initiatives to begin implementation in January 2027. General responses with generic capability statements that do not address the specific content of this RFI may not be considered. Training Consultation for Program Revision Describe the largest training program for which your company has been a training consultant. description: Request for SF 330 Submissions for A-E Construction Management Services-GAOA SEWER at MIDWAY ATOLL NWR. This is a request for SF 330 submissions only, DO NOT SUBMIT PROPOSALS AT THIS TIME. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) is seeking qualification statements from Architect-Engineering firms for construction management services which include support during solicitation of the Consolidated Projects on Midway Atoll National Wildlife Refuge (NWR), refer to the Statement of Work (SOW) for task breakdown. The project takes place on Midway Atoll NWR, which is in the North Pacific Ocean. Refer to attachments for submission requirements, evaluation criteria, work requirements, and other important information. Instructions to Firms: Refer to attached Request for SF 330 Submissions for detailed information. Firms that meet the requirements described in the attached Request for SF 330 Submissions are invited to complete a SF 330 Package. The form can be sourced from https://www.gsa.gov/portal/forms/download/116486 The only acceptable method of submission is by email to CO at shanen_fox@ios.doi.gov by the required deadline. Extensions will not be granted unless the CO determines it�s in the best interest of the Government. Contracting Officer/Point of Contact: All inquiries regarding this announcement must be submitted in writing via email only, by the required question deadline. No calls will be returned as all inquiries must be submitted via email. Shanen Fox, Email: shanen_fox@ios.doi.gov Questions and Inquiries: Contact Shanen Fox, Contracting Officer. Contact may be made via email to shanen_fox@ios.doi.gov. All inquiries and questions shall be submitted in writing via email only by the cutoff date and time listed above. Nothing in this request is changed unless an amendment is posted to sam.gov as an amendment prior to submission. Contract Structure: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) intends to award one firm-fixed price contract for Architect-Engineering Services. Required SAM Registration: To be eligible for contract award, a firm must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) and active by the closing of this announcement. Failure to register in SAM.gov may render a firm ineligible for award. SAM registration is free of charge and can be completed at www.sam.gov. SELECTION OF THE MOST HIGHLY QUALIFIED FIRMS AFTER SF 330 EVALUATIONS: Following the board�s evaluation of SF330s, selection of up to five (5) of the most highly qualified firms will be determined and discussions will be held with these firms in accordance with FAR 36.602-1 (c). All firms of the most highly qualified firms will be asked similar questions, which may include topics such as experience, capabilities, capacity, organization, management, quality control procedures, and approach for the project, as appropriate. Following completion of discussions, the board will select the most highly qualified firm. A Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued to the most highly qualified firm with award of one firm-fixed price contract if a fair and reasonable price can be agreed upon. If a fair and reasonable price cannot be agreed upon, the Service will move to negotiations with the next highest ranked firm. This process will continue until award can be made to the highest ranked firm providing a fair and reasonable price.

title: Interactive Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) Training Platform Development
description: Request for Information (RFI) & Sources Sought (pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations- Part 5) Interactive Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) Training Platform Development Issued By: Department of Transportation | Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) Date of Issue: September 9, 2026 Response Deadline: September 28, 2026 SIC/Product Service Code: 7373 Computer Integrated Systems NAICS Code: 541511 Custom Computer Programming Services 1. Introduction The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) is seeking information from interested parties and potential vendors regarding the development of an Interactive LNG Training Platform. The interactive, virtual LNG plant training platform should allow users to perform virtual plant walkdowns, review piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), and visualize process flows through the internal components of critical machinery (e.g., valves, vessels, pumps, compressors). This RFI is intended for market research purposes only and supports ongoing agency acquisition planning aligned with modern federal procurement principles. 2. Project Background and Goals PHMSA is committed to enhancing the safety and oversight of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) facilities. The objective of this project is to create a digital, high-fidelity, and interactive training environment that allows inspectors to simulate complex operational scenarios and safety inspections. Key goals include: Improving technical competency in LNG facility oversight. Utilizing 3D immersive technologies and digital twin capabilities to bridge the gap between classroom and field. Creating a scalable, modular curriculum that evolves with regulatory standards. Maximizing the leverage of commercial solutions and modern cloud infrastructure. 3. Key Information Requested PHMSA requests that interested respondents provide detailed information on the following categories: 3.1 Company Profile & Administrative Information Please complete the following table to assist PHMSA in market research and business size determination: Company Name Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) CAGE Code Socioeconomic Business Size (e.g., SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, HUBZone, Small, Large) Point of Contact Information (Name, Email, Phone) [Vendor Name] [12-character UEI] [5-charac ter CAGE] t[Socioeconomic Status] [Name, Email, Phone] Small Business Capacity: If identified as a small business, please state whether your firm possesses the internal capacity and capability to perform as the prime contractor for a project of this scope or if teaming/subcontracting arrangements would be necessary. 3.2 Technical Capabilities & Innovation Describe your firm�s experience in developing high-fidelity 3D simulations or "Digital Twins" for industrial facilities. What hardware and software requirements do you typically recommend for a platform of this scale? Explain your approach to ensuring interactivity and user engagement within a training module. Commerciality & COTS Analysis: To what extent can your proposed solution leverage existing Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software components, modular training engines, or commercial 3D/VR frameworks versus requiring custom government-unique software development? 3.3 Content and Curriculum Design How do you approach mapping technical regulatory requirements (e.g., 49 CFR Part 193) into interactive learning objectives? Describe your capability to develop branching scenarios where trainee decisions lead to different safety outcomes. 3.4 Cybersecurity, Hosting & Data Rights Deployment & Cloud Posture: Describe your solution's typical deployment model (e.g., SaaS, FedRAMP-authorized Cloud, On-Premise, Hybrid) and compatibility with federal cybersecurity frameworks (FAR Part 40 / CUI handling). Intellectual Property & Licensing: Describe your standard licensing structure and approach to data rights for custom-developed 3D models, code, and scenario content (e.g., proprietary licensing vs. Government Purpose Rights / Unlimited Rights). 3.5 Past Performance Please provide details on up to three (3) recent projects of similar scope and complexity: Project Title Client Type (Gov/Private) Core Technology Used Year Completed [Project 1] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] [Project 2] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] [Project 3] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] 3.6 Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) and Timeline Provide a non-binding estimate of the typical timeline for developing a comprehensive training platform with 5�10 high-complexity modules. Outline standard pricing models (e.g., fixed-price development, recurring licensing fees, maintenance, and ongoing support). 4. Submission Instructions & Industry Engagement Responses should be submitted in electronic format to the point of contact listed below. Please limit technical responses to 20 pages, excluding company brochures or supplemental past performance data. Industry Engagement / Vendor Demos: PHMSA may, at its discretion, invite select respondents to participate in virtual demonstrations or technical exchange sessions to further inform agency acquisition planning. USDOT Point of Contact: Loni Chinn Email: loni.chinn@dot.gov 5. Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. PHMSA will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI.

title: TR-143A TRANSDUCERS
description: ITEM DESCRIPTION - Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane (NSWC Crane) has a requirement to procure TR-143A Transducers, Part Number: 7146100-302. These transducers are utilized in the SP24 Trident Navigation Subsystem, supporting United States (U.S) Navy and United Kingdom (UK) Ballistic Missile Submarine Nuclear Powered submarines as part of the Navigation Subsystem Sonar. These transducers are used in coordination with TR-333 Hydrophones to receive signals from the ocean floor and to improve submarine launch accuracy. The transducers are manufactured items used as replacement assets during normal refit, replenish, and replacement operations for the SP24 Trident Navigation Subsystem and support U.S. Ohio and Columbia class submarines in addition to UK Vanguard and Dreadnought class submarines. The proposed contract action is for a two-year ordering period extension and ceiling increase, on contract N0016426DGP87, a firm-fixed-price, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity contract with a five-year ordering period. The contract is for supplies which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, Massa Products Corporation, Hingham, MA 02043 (CAGE 88958), under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.103-1 (c) (2), only one responsible source. The requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis, because the supplies have been deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a follow-on contract for the continued production of highly specialized equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that award to any other source would result in (A) Substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition or (B) Unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Additionally, the Government is pursuing a sole source procurement to mitigate associated certification costs and certification testing that can take up to thirty-six months to complete. Furthermore, if a potential vendor is not capable of meeting the certification requirements, there is high likelihood that ship schedules will be significantly impacted. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract extension based upon responses to the solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of re-evaluating the justification for sole source or limitation of sources and making a determination to change the acquisition strategy to a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov.

title: Pre-solicitation Notice: RRC Services to be Located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement Radius 150-mile not Restricted by State or County Lines
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC26R00000014 Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement Radius 150-mile not Restricted by State or County Lines The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement radius 150-mile not restricted by State or County lines. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 14 beds (12 males and 2 females) for the base year and an estimated maximum 35 beds (30 males and 5 females) facility. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 10 placements (for the base year) and an estimated maximum 25 placements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000014 will be available on or about September 29, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. Future information about this acquisition will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The estimated closing date of this solicitation (RFP) will be after 60 days around November 30, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC26R00000014 Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement Radius 150-mile not Restricted by State or County Lines The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement radius 150-mile not restricted by State or County lines. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 14 beds (12 males and 2 females) for the base year and an estimated maximum 35 beds (30 males and 5 females) for female facility. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 10 placements (for the base year) and an estimated maximum 25 placements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000014 will be available on or about September 29, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. Future information about this acquisition will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The estimated closing date of this solicitation (RFP) will be after 60 days around November 30, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

Cooperative Driving Automation (CDA) Small-Scale Industry Prototype
description: UPDATE: On August 24, 2026 a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) amendment was issued, see amended BAA in the attachments section titled "693JJ3-26-BAA-0005_A00001_CDA Prototype". Additionally, the complete Q&A was posted as a PDF titled "Q A - Complete". Note that the due date for proposals was extended. BACKGROUND: USDOT envisions a future transportation ecosystem where CDA complements both human-driven and automated vehicles to improve roadway safety, mobility, and operational efficiency. While standalone vehicle automation has advanced, it continues to struggle with complex edge cases such as occlusion, complex merging, or identifying pedestrians hidden behind buildings at corners, and vehicle sensors alone cannot adequately resolve these issues. Prior USDOT-supported research projects have successfully demonstrated the technical proof-of-concept at technology readiness levels (TRL) of 3-5 for CDA applications in laboratory and closed environments. However, most new vehicles are not equipped with CDA capabilities and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) remain reluctant to integrate these technologies into production lines due to a lack of consumer awareness and unclear regulatory, policy, and institutional frameworks. This acquisition seeks to build on foundational CDA research by bridging the gap between research concepts and commercial viability. There is a critical need to develop and test pre-production, industry-led prototypes at a TRL of 6-7, to validate that the data shared between vehicles and roadside infrastructure is accurate, secure, and reliable enough to support functional safety. By demonstrating CDA technologies in operational conditions, researchers will gain a better understanding of cooperative systems and if they are more valuable in terms of improving roadway safety, than standalone automation or vehicle-to-everything (V2X) technologies alone. PURPOSE: The purpose of this requirement is to demonstrate industry-led CDA prototypes in controlled and real-world conditions in order to generate data-driven insights that will support the development of a national strategy to deploy CDA across rural, suburban, and urban roadway systems. This effort prioritizes industry-ready CDA technology for use cases with clear safety and/or mobility benefit potential, specifically focusing on: (1) Work Zone Management, (2) Traffic Incident Management, (3) Cooperative Perception, and/or (4) Emergency/Transit Vehicle Awareness. Contractors will first validate the prototype's interoperability, functional safety, and cybersecurity in a relevant, controlled testbed environment. Following successful controlled testing, the effort will progress into a small scale real-world demonstration on public roads with mixed traffic to validate operational readiness and generate data-driven insights.

title: C1DA--A/E Services Replace Patient Lifts B331, B348, & B360 Project Number: 640A0-27-103
description: This is a Call for SF 330s. Please read the entire document. The Department of Veterans Affairs VA Palo Alto Menlo Park Healthcare System, CA is seeking Architectural/Engineering Firms to submit Standard Form (SF) 330 for Project 640A0-27-103, Replace Patient Lifts B331, B348, & B360. The project will be located at the Palo Alto Menlo Park VA Campus, 3801 Miranda Ave, Palo Alto, California 94304. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The VA Palo Alto - Menlo Park Division needs A/E design services to replace/install 141 new ceiling-mounted patient lifts and extend 24 existing lifts for full room + bathroom coverage in CLC Buildings 331, 348, and 360. B348/B360 private rooms have no lift; B331 has outdated linear lifts; B360 needs bathroom coverage extensions + 30 motor upgrades. A/E Requirement: Full field survey above/below ceiling, structural/SE seismic analysis and HCAI OPM, MEP/electrical, fire protection, phasing plan for occupied patient rooms, Revit BIM, specs, and independent cost estimate. Construction cost shall not exceed $16.4M for all work in B331, B348 & B360, requiring site investigations, block diagrams, and full design deliverables at 35%, 65%, 95%, 100% and final production per VA Master Specs and all applicable codes, including cost estimates, phased construction documents, and 5-year construction period services including RFI responses, submittal reviews, weekly meetings, site inspections, and as-builts, all to be completed within a 266-day design period. The design shall also substantially meet the VA design criteria as listed in VA design guides and manuals, which can be found on the web at the VA Office of Facilities Management technical information library site address: http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL The design effort shall also include review of and assurance of compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act, including development and submission of all documents, reports, and activities necessary to obtain the required compliance. The contract work requires multiple disciplines. The Prime firm shall be a licensed/registered professional firm in any state in the United States, and the lead designer in each discipline must be registered/licensed in any state. Exception: The Structural Engineer of Record (SEOR) participating in the structural/seismic design must be licensed in the State of California and must have current authority to use the title of Structural Engineer (SE) in California, per H-18-8 and VA Directive 7512. Disciplines required include, but are not limited to: Architectural, Civil, Interior Design, Structural (CA SE), HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical, Fire Protection, Construction Cost Estimating, Signage/Wayfinding, Landscaping and Geotechnical. Include any additional disciplines that may be necessary on SF 330. SF 330 Part 1F Example Projects; present all relevant VA projects first. Include in block 21 the contract number for all federal projects. Do not include the CPARS reports for federal projects. SELECTION CRITERIA Selection of firms for interviews and negotiations shall be based on an evaluation of the submitted SF-330s based on the selection criteria listed below in a descending order of precedence. SF-330s, Part I may be accompanied by any other evidence of experience and capabilities the applicant considers relevant. Part II shall be submitted for each proposed consultant s office involved. Additional Evaluation Factors: Previous experience with patient lift design in a hospital setting and length of and role in that experience. If no patient lift design, then required hospital setting design experience and associated phasing requirements in an occupied Community Living Center (CLC) / acute care environment. Experience with patient lift products, makers, and providers (e.g., ARJO and similar ceiling-mounted systems) is desired and will be evaluated. Design for construction staging/phasing in an active, occupied healthcare environment, including ICRA/ILSM measures, is required. Selection Criteria descriptions are provided below. Experience of the prime firm, consultant firms, and proposed designers. Prime firms must have proven experience in health care design through construction administration. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence in hospital design with the ability to design and administer projects within a complex, active healthcare environment with stringent seismic requirements in the State of California. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time and the ability to adhere to schedules. Provide current workload capability of the prime firm, proposed consultants, and designers. Literature should be included to demonstrate the prime firm s ability to meet scheduled deadlines. This will allow the Government to determine the availability of experienced personnel during the performance period of the contract as well as the capacity to complete the work required. Past Performance on contracts with respect to cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules during design and construction phases (prime firm). Geographical location and knowledge of the locality of the project. This requirement considers the prime firm s familiarity with the applicable geographic area s architectural standards and codes, building codes, environmental regulations, soil conditions, and seismic requirements within the Palo Alto Menlo Park area. The prime firm must be able to respond to and be on-site within a twenty-four-hour window. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: No more than eighty (80) pages Font size no smaller than 10 Size of emails not to exceed 10 MB. If more than one email is sent, number the emails in the subject line as 1 of 2, 2 of 2. Complete and return VAAR 852.219-76 VA Notice of Limitation on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (attached) Subject line of the email shall state Company Name | Response to 36C26126Q1139_1 | email 1 of 2 (if necessary). In the body of the email, include Prime Company Name; UEI Number; email address and phone number of primary points of contact. DUE DATE FOR SF 330 Firms that meet the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit required SF 330s by 12:00 P.M. (PDT) Monday, September 28, 2026, to Alex Arter at alex.arter@va.gov. It is the intent of the Contracting Officer to make a single firm-fixed-price contract award under this solicitation.

description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION ITEM: Undershirt, Olive Drab, MC PGC: 02424--NSN: 8420-01-450-0048(s) EA Specification/CID: A-A-50013H, dated September 9, 2024 RFP SPE1C1-26-R-0101 will be utilized for the purchase of item UNDERSHIRT, OLIVE DRAB, MC. This proposed buy will result in a negotiated Indefinite Delivery Type contract(s). This acquisition is a 60-month contract consisting of five (5) 12-month price tier periods. The quantities will be as follows: Quantity Total Acquisition: Contract Guaranteed Min: 55,776 each Annual Estimated Quantity: 222,816 each per tier Contract Maximum: 1,392,600 each all tiers combined The resultant contract(s) will have a Five (5) year ordering period. Within the Five (5) year ordering period, there will be Five (5) 12-month price Tier periods. This proposed buy will result in a negotiated Indefinite Delivery Type Contract(s). The quantities for the acquisition are listed above for the total acquisition. This proposed buy will result with the intent of the Government to award up to one (1) negotiated Indefinite Delivery Type contract. Best Value / Trade Off / Source Selection Procedures will be utilized in making the proposed award(s), and as a result, Technical Proposals are required. Technical and Past Performance, when combined, are more important than cost or price. Evaluation factors are as follows in descending order of importance: Product Demonstration Model (PDM) in accordance with CID A-A-50013H, dated September 9, 2024 and Past Performance/Performance Confidence Assessment. Evaluation of the PDMs will effectively indicate the contractor�s comprehension of the item�s technical requirements and their ability to manufacture the items in accordance with the Purchase Description. title: C1DA--A/E Services Replace Patient Lifts B331, B348, & B360 Project Number: 640A0-27-103
description: This is a Call for SF 330s. Please read the entire document. The Department of Veterans Affairs VA Palo Alto Menlo Park Healthcare System, CA is seeking Architectural/Engineering Firms to submit Standard Form (SF) 330 for Project 640A0-27-103, Replace Patient Lifts B331, B348, & B360. The project will be located at the Palo Alto Menlo Park VA Campus, 3801 Miranda Ave, Palo Alto, California 94304. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The VA Palo Alto - Menlo Park Division needs A/E design services to replace/install 141 new ceiling-mounted patient lifts and extend 24 existing lifts for full room + bathroom coverage in CLC Buildings 331, 348, and 360. B348/B360 private rooms have no lift; B331 has outdated linear lifts; B360 needs bathroom coverage extensions + 30 motor upgrades. A/E Requirement: Full field survey above/below ceiling, structural/SE seismic analysis and HCAI OPM, MEP/electrical, fire protection, phasing plan for occupied patient rooms, Revit BIM, specs, and independent cost estimate. Construction cost shall not exceed $16.4M for all work in B331, B348 & B360, requiring site investigations, block diagrams, and full design deliverables at 35%, 65%, 95%, 100% and final production per VA Master Specs and all applicable codes, including cost estimates, phased construction documents, and 5-year construction period services including RFI responses, submittal reviews, weekly meetings, site inspections, and as-builts, all to be completed within a 266-day design period. The design shall also substantially meet the VA design criteria as listed in VA design guides and manuals, which can be found on the web at the VA Office of Facilities Management technical information library site address: http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL The design effort shall also include review of and assurance of compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act, including development and submission of all documents, reports, and activities necessary to obtain the required compliance. The contract work requires multiple disciplines. The Prime firm shall be a licensed/registered professional firm in any state in the United States, and the lead designer in each discipline must be registered/licensed in any state. Exception: The Structural Engineer of Record (SEOR) participating in the structural/seismic design must be licensed in the State of California and must have current authority to use the title of Structural Engineer (SE) in California, per H-18-8 and VA Directive 7512. Disciplines required include, but are not limited to: Architectural, Civil, Interior Design, Structural (CA SE), HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical, Fire Protection, Construction Cost Estimating, Signage/Wayfinding, Landscaping and Geotechnical. Include any additional disciplines that may be necessary on SF 330. SF 330 Part 1F Example Projects; present all relevant VA projects first. Include in block 21 the contract number for all federal projects. Do not include the CPARS reports for federal projects. SELECTION CRITERIA Selection of firms for interviews and negotiations shall be based on an evaluation of the submitted SF-330s based on the selection criteria listed below in a descending order of precedence. SF-330s, Part I may be accompanied by any other evidence of experience and capabilities the applicant considers relevant. Part II shall be submitted for each proposed consultant s office involved. Additional Evaluation Factors: Previous experience with patient lift design in a hospital setting and length of and role in that experience. If no patient lift design, then required hospital setting design experience and associated phasing requirements in an occupied Community Living Center (CLC) / acute care environment. Experience with patient lift products, makers, and providers (e.g., ARJO and similar ceiling-mounted systems) is desired and will be evaluated. Design for construction staging/phasing in an active, occupied healthcare environment, including ICRA/ILSM measures, is required. Selection Criteria descriptions are provided below. Experience of the prime firm, consultant firms, and proposed designers. Prime firms must have proven experience in health care design through construction administration. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence in hospital design with the ability to design and administer projects within a complex, active healthcare environment with stringent seismic requirements in the State of California. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time and the ability to adhere to schedules. Provide current workload capability of the prime firm, proposed consultants, and designers. Literature should be included to demonstrate the prime firm s ability to meet scheduled deadlines. This will allow the Government to determine the availability of experienced personnel during the performance period of the contract as well as the capacity to complete the work required. Past Performance on contracts with respect to cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules during design and construction phases (prime firm). Geographical location and knowledge of the locality of the project. This requirement considers the prime firm s familiarity with the applicable geographic area s architectural standards and codes, building codes, environmental regulations, soil conditions, and seismic requirements within the Palo Alto Menlo Park area. The prime firm must be able to respond to and be on-site within a twenty-four-hour window. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: No more than eighty (80) pages Font size no smaller than 10 Size of emails not to exceed 10 MB. If more than one email is sent, number the emails in the subject line as 1 of 2, 2 of 2. Complete and return VAAR 852.219-76 VA Notice of Limitation on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (attached) Subject line of the email shall state Company Name | Response to 36C26126Q1139_1 | email 1 of 2 (if necessary). In the body of the email, include Prime Company Name; UEI Number; email address and phone number of primary points of contact. DUE DATE FOR SF 330 Firms that meet the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit required SF 330s by 12:00 P.M. (PDT) Monday, September 28, 2026, to Alex Arter at alex.arter@va.gov. It is the intent of the Contracting Officer to make a single firm-fixed-price contract award under this solicitation.

title: KC135 Anti Collision Strobe Light
description: The KC-135 anti-collision strobe lights are high density dual color strobe lights and are mounted on the top and bottom of the fuselage. The strobe lights flash at a rate of 45 � 60 flashes per minute. They are powered by separate power supplies. For the upper strobe light, the power supply is located inside the fuselage below the strobe light, mounted on the side of the air conditioning duct. For the lower strobe light, the power supply is located in the keel beam on standard tankers or mounted on the side of an air conditioning duct in the upper part of fuselage for remaining aircraft. Each power supply is powered by 28 Vdc.

PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number.
